FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A45
Press the clutch fully down and select a lower gear; abrupt deceleration may require skipping to an even lower gear. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A45
After selecting a lower gear, release the clutch toward its friction point while adding accelerator pressure as needed. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A45
To hold a manual vehicle for an uphill start, set the parking brake, depress the clutch and choose first gear. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A45
For an uphill start, ease the clutch to engagement with gentle acceleration and release the parking brake when the vehicle begins pulling forward. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A45
Continue accelerating in first gear during the uphill start until there is enough speed to shift to second. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A45
Before stopping, check rear traffic in the mirrors, move to the brake and apply smooth, steady pressure. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A45
When stopping a manual vehicle, depress the clutch as the vehicle comes to a halt. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A46
For an unexpected slowdown or stop, quickly tap the brake pedal 3 or 4 times to alert the driver behind. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A46
Turn the steering wheel toward the intended direction in forward travel and in reverse. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A46
Use the 9-and-3 or 8-and-4 hand positions for steering control and reduced airbag-injury risk. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A46
Hold the wheel firmly but gently with the fingers, keeping the thumbs along its face and avoiding a grip on the inside rim. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A46
Check behind the vehicle before entering because small objects and children can be hidden from the driver’s seat. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A46
To begin backing, start the vehicle, apply the brake and select reverse. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A46
For backing, place the left hand at 12 o’clock, rest the right arm behind the passenger seat and look through the rear window. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A46
Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup camera when reversing; each leaves part of the rear area unseen. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A46
Back no faster than a slow walking pace and steer toward the intended movement of the vehicle’s rear. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A46
When turning in reverse, make brief checks ahead and to the sides while continuing to look rearward until fully stopped. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A46
Minimize backing and avoid reversing into traffic. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A46
Back into a driveway or parking space unless signs prohibit it so you can leave facing forward. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A47
The handbook advises limiting idling around a start or stop to 1 minute. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A47
Gentle driving during the first few minutes warms the engine more efficiently than extended idling. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A47
Idling wastes fuel and releases harmful pollutants. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A47
Some Maine local governments have ordinances restricting idling. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]
